distribution.title:
Results from tuber samples analysed at three stages: fresh, after freeze-drying (using in-house lyophilization equipment), and after 12 months of storage.
Analyses will include: a) starch profiling (total starch content in fresh tubers will be determined using the specific gravity method, and the results will be used to improve NIR calibrations for starch assessment in freeze-dried potato samples. Resistant starch, amylose/amylopectin ratio via chemical methods and spectrophotometry), b) protein analysis (NIRS express analysis supported by updated calibrations developed during the project), c) vitamin C analysis using HPLC methods.

Trials will be carried out under both integrated and organic farming systems. distribution.title: Empirical data collection from field trials at AREI Priekuli using approximately 15 potato genotypes selected from prior breeding research will ensure first results before biochemical analyses. These trials will also provide baseline agronomic data essential for evaluation of genotype × environment × processing interactions. Trials will be carried out under both integrated and organic farming systems. Agronomic data will be collected, including plant development stages, chlorophyll content (SPAD), yield, and tuber dry matter and starch content. Empirical findings will be combined with prior genotype datasets to enrich interpretation. Statistical models will be used to assess trait dynamics across growing systems and processing stages, to identify which specific genotype-related traits contribute most to nutrient retention and biochemical stability during and after freeze-drying.

dataset.title: Field trials of potato genotypes

dmp.description:
DMP with appropriate metadata and licensing to support reuse by researchers, plant breeders, and food industry stakeholders. Version control and persistent identifiers (DOIs) will ensure traceability. Through the research project, two datasets will be created to implement all the data from field trials and laboratory experiments. Both datasets will be openly available (open access) after publishing according to the FAIR principles. The datasets will provide information for potato processors and other researchers to use in their studies.
This project aims to identify potato genotypes with high nutritional value after freeze-drying and storage, contributing to the development of a food safety system. The knowledge gained will contribute to the development of high-quality, long-term storage products for national food reserves, emergencies and active lifestyles.
Main tasks:
1) To assess the development characteristics of potato genotypes, yield and quality in different growing systems;
2) To determine the dynamics of biochemical characteristics characterizing quality – starch, protein content and vitamin content before and after lyophilization and after storage;
3) Perform and evaluate the structure of potato starch by determining the resistant starch content and the amylose-amylopectin ratio;
4) To evaluate the impact of genotype and cultivation system interaction on the quality parameters of freeze-dried products, identifying genotypes with equivalent nutritional value after freeze-drying, and to provide information to the public about the results obtained in scientific publications, conference reports, and local educational events.
Project innovation:
In contrast to recent efforts to develop products that meet consumer requirements, this project focuses on the biochemical and agronomic rationale for maintaining nutritional value in the long term, contributing to the development of functional foods, improving food reserve strategies, and advancing the breeding process.
1) Research direction - assessment of biochemical traits based on the interaction of genotype × environment × processing type;
2) Development of a methodology for improving the breeding process – adaptation of analytical and express technologies for evaluating nutritional elements ;
3) Focusing the strategy, changing the emphasis from the evaluation of the final product to the identification of the most optimal genotype traits for processing, in order to maintain the nutritional value of the processed product for a long time, already during the breeding process.
